name: Calibration-aware risk estimation
notes: Calibration-focused Pima work already exists (calib_first_rs preprint, leakfree_rs preprint, reliab_aware). Calibration is under-reported in general (christodoulou 79%), but that is not a Pima gap.

name: Decision-threshold trade-off analysis
notes: thresh_math sweeps thresholds 0.30-0.70 on Pima with repeated leakage-free CV; wynants2019 argues thresholds are ad hoc. Screening-sensitivity-target thresholds with uncertainty not seen, but incremental.

name: Explanation stability (local SHAP / importance)
notes: Heavily covered: jaimlnn (permutation importance on Pima, resampling), zenodo_shap, attrimp/hypclass/stablerank preprints, JBHI Rashomon, krishna, alvarez. For logistic regression, interventional SHAP is analytic (beta_j x (x_j - background mean)), so stability is expected to be high and the result trivial.

name: Multi-family performance + calibration comparison
notes: Already done repeatedly (aposta, leakfree_rs, jaimlnn, etasr); christodoulou shows LR is competitive in general.

name: Robustness to missingness / perturbation (as originally defined)
notes: General clinical-prediction missing-data methodology is strong (sisk2023, jce2024imp, sim2025, sperrin2020); explainability under imputation has a Twente conference paper and a 2026 thesis; msys studied Pima zeros. Only a Pima-specific application would remain.

name: Why Pima results may not generalise (documentary + external)
notes: Needs external datasets with compatible features (none in the project) and the 1988 paper's full text for outcome timing (unread). Cross-dataset work exists but with different feature sets (aposta).

name: Integrated reproducible evaluation framework
notes: leakfree_rs, aposta, etasr, reliab_aware already present 'frameworks'; integration alone is not a defensible novelty claim.

name: Reporting/leakage audit of Pima-based ML papers
notes: No Pima-specific audit found (search not exhaustive); audits exist elsewhere (kapoor, christodoulou). Needs systematic search + full texts; meta-research rather than a method, which may not satisfy a 'methodological contribution' expectation.

name: Label-aware imputation as a leakage source: quantify inflation and detect it (canary diagnostic)
notes: Three Pima studies describe outcome-conditional imputation (msys 'group median'; pima_leaksafe 'class-conditional medians'; Khan 2026 'group-median') and report AUC 0.93-0.956, far above leakage-safe 0.83-0.85; no study quantifying this mechanism was found (not exhaustive). Exploratory pilot (training split only): RF AUC 0.840 -> 0.938 with the leaky pipeline; label-permutation canary 0.49 (valid) vs 0.857 (leaky).
